subtitle: In the shadow of Chittor, a nameless founder walks between stone and song

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a lone warrior-king silhouetted against Chittor fort and a sky of fading stars
panels.action: Bappa Rawal stands on a rocky ridge before the looming walls of Chittor, his silhouette caught between the ancient stone fort and a vast Rajasthani sky that fades from night into dawn.

dialogue.text: Mewar sings of Bappa Rawal, its first great hero—yet in the earliest stone records of his own house, the founder they praise has no name.

i18n.hi: मेवाड़ बप्पा रावल को पहला महान नायक गाता है—पर उनकी ही वंश-लिपि की सबसे पुरानी शिला में जिस संस्थापक की स्तुति है, उसका नाम नहीं है।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from chisel on stone to reveal a 10th-century inscription wall
panels.action: A close hand chisels Devanagari letters into a sandstone slab, the camera revealing a long inscription panel set in the wall of a modest shrine at Atpur in Medapata.

dialogue.text: We begin not with legend, but with stone. At Atpur, in 977, a mason cuts the Guhila line into rock, fixing for the first time a royal past that will outlive all men who breathe it.

i18n.hi: कहानी नहीं, पत्थर से शुरू करते हैं। ९७७ में आतपुर पर एक राजमिस्त्री गुहिल वंश काटता है, पहली बार शिला पर वो राजवंश गढ़ता है जो सब सांसों से लंबा जिएगा।

panels.shot: top-down shot of the Atpur inscription surrounded by palm-leaf manuscripts and a scholar’s hands
panels.action: On a scholar’s floor, a rubbing of the Atpur inscription lies beside palm-leaf manuscripts, oil lamps, and a careful hand tracing names in the genealogy with a reed pen.

dialogue.text: Name after name marches down the Atpur slab. The Guhilas of Ahar and Medapata speak clearly: fathers, sons, donors, dates. Yet the name that haunts Mewar today is missing.

i18n.hi: नाम पर नाम आतपुर की पटिया पर उतरते जाते हैं। आहर और मेड़पाट के गुहिल साफ बोलते हैं: पिता, पुत्र, दाता, तिथि। पर आज मेवाड़ को जो नाम सताता है, वो कहीं नहीं है।

panels.shot: cross-dissolve style composition: half frame ancient inscription, half frame heroic bardic Bappa on horseback
panels.action: One half of the panel shows lines of the Atpur inscription; the other half, a bardic vision of Bappa Rawal astride a horse, banner streaming, riding across the Aravalli hills.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, court bards will call that founder Bappa Rawal, rider of the Aravallis, seizer of Chittor. But the stone of 977 does not speak his name at all.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद दरबारी चारण उसी संस्थापक को बप्पा रावल कहेंगे—अरावली का घुड़सवार, चित्तौड़ का विजेता। पर ९७७ की वही शिला उसका नाम तक नहीं कहती।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Ahar and the plains of Medapata with early-medieval settlements
panels.action: A landscape of early-medieval Rajasthan unfolds: clustered houses around the town of Ahar, fields along a river, small shrines, and the low ripple of the Aravalli range in the distance.

dialogue.text: Their world was Ahar and Medapata, not yet the full sweep of later Mewar. Villages hugged tanks and streams, shrines rose to local deities, and the Guhilas grew in the shadow of larger powers.

i18n.hi: तब उनकी दुनिया बस आहर और मेड़पाट थी, अभी का फैला हुआ मेवाड़ नहीं। गाँव तालाबों और नालों से चिपके थे, देसी देवताओं के थान उठ रहे थे, और गुहिल बड़े राजों की छांव में बढ़ रहे थे।

panels.shot: high-angle view of an 8th-century court with a modest chief receiving envoys
panels.action: Inside a simple pillared hall, an early Guhila chief sits on a low seat, listening as envoys from neighbouring clans and perhaps a far-off imperial emissary bow and present gifts.

dialogue.text: Earlier still, before inscriptions, Guhila leaders ruled as local chiefs. Their names survive fragmentary, their alliances and quarrels hinted at only by later praise and the pattern of land grants.

i18n.hi: उससे भी पहले, जब शिलालेख नहीं थे, गुहिल सरदार बस देसी मुखिया थे। नाम टुकड़ों में बचे हैं, उनके मेल-जोल और झगड़े बस बाद की स्तुतियों और बँटाई हुई ज़मीन के नक्शे से झलकते हैं।

panels.shot: dramatic mid-shot of Bappa Rawal as imagined by a 15th-century bard in Rana Kumbha’s court
panels.action: In a richly lit 15th-century hall, a bard gestures grandly as he describes Bappa Rawal; in his tale-vision, Bappa stands young and resolute, sword sheathed, eyes fixed on a distant fortress.

dialogue.text: By Rana Kumbha’s time, bards in Udaipur and Kumbhalgarh had shaped one Guhila into Bappa Rawal—the youth who rose from obscurity and became the archetype of a Rajput founder.

i18n.hi: राणा कुम्भा के ज़माने तक, उदयपुर और कुम्भलगढ़ के भाटों ने एक गुहिल को गढ़कर बप्पा रावल बनाया—वो छोरा जो गुमनामी से उठा और आदर्श राजपूत संस्थापक बन गया।

panels.shot: low-angle tracking shot of Bappa walking through a shrine to Eklingji, lit by lamps
panels.action: Bappa Rawal walks bareheaded into a stone shrine of Eklingji, its interior lit by rows of oil lamps and incense haze, his face a mix of awe and determination as he approaches the linga.

dialogue.text: Tradition brings in sage Harit Rashi and the god Eklingji. In bardic song, Bappa is blessed in this shrine, bound to serve the deity as vassal even as he rules men as king.

i18n.hi: परंपरा में ऋषि हरित राशी और देव एकलिंगजी आते हैं। भाटों के पदों में बप्पा इसी देवालय में आशीर्वाद पाता है, देव का जागीरदार बनकर, और लोगों पर राजा बनकर राज करता है।

panels.shot: contrast shot: one side shows the Eklingji temple, the other a scholar annotating 'later tradition'
panels.action: On one side, devotees throng an Eklingji shrine, holding lamps; on the other, a modern historian at a desk under a lamp writes notes, the words 'later bardic tradition' circled on a page.

dialogue.text: These stories have power, but they come from later prashastis and court memory. The inscriptions themselves are silent on Harit Rashi, on visions in the temple, on the god’s direct gift of Chittor.

i18n.hi: ये कथाएँ असरदार हैं, पर आती हैं बाद की प्रशस्तियों और दरबारी यादों से। खुद शिलालेख हरित राशी पर चुप हैं, मंदिर के दर्शन पर चुप हैं, और देव से सीधे चित्तौड़ मिलने की बात पर भी।

panels.shot: wide battle-table shot with Bappa and allies around a rough map of Chittor and Medapata
panels.action: Bappa stands at a rough wooden table where a hand-drawn map shows Chittor atop its hill and the plains of Medapata around it, while armoured companions watch his hand trace possible routes.

dialogue.text: Later tradition dates his seizure of Chittor to around 728 or 734, in an age of shifting powers. Arab armies tested the western frontiers, Pratiharas and other houses vied across north India.

i18n.hi: बाद की परंपरा उसके चित्तौड़ हरण को करीब ७२८ या ७३४ के आस-पास रखती है, जब ताकतें बदल रही थीं। अरब लश्कर पश्चिमी सरहद टटोल रहे थे, प्रतिहार और दूसरी नसलें उत्तर भारत में भिड़ रहीं थीं।

panels.shot: distant wide shot of Bappa’s forces climbing towards Chittor’s plateau at dawn
panels.action: In the pale light of dawn, a small force led by Bappa ascends the winding path up to Chittor’s plateau, banners low, horses and men moving cautiously along the rugged incline.

dialogue.text: Stories speak of Bappa taking Chittor in a daring stroke. Yet the stones of Chittor itself fall quiet for long stretches; clear Guhila control shines only from inscriptions of the mid-tenth century.

i18n.hi: कहानियाँ कहती हैं कि बप्पा ने चित्तौड़ पर अचानक धावा बोला। पर खुद चित्तौड़ की शिलाएँ लंबे अरसे खामोश रहती हैं; साफ गुहिल हुकूमत तो दसवीं सदी के बीच के अभिलेखों से ही चमकती है।

panels.shot: time-lapse style composite of Chittor fort across centuries with changing banners
panels.action: Chittor’s massive walls remain constant as the sky and foreground change, showing different dynastic banners rising and falling over the fort across three stylised moments in time.

dialogue.text: Between legend and epigraphy lies a long, uncertain time. Chittor may have changed hands, stood contested, or lay under other houses’ banners before Guhila rule emerges firmly on record.

i18n.hi: कथा और शिलालेख के बीच लंबा, धुंधला ज़माना पड़ा है। हो सकता है चित्तौड़ कई बार हाथ बदले, झगड़े में रहा, या दूसरे घरानों के झंडे तले रहा, इससे पहले कि गुहिल राज साफ़-साफ़ दिखे।

panels.shot: close-up of the Kumbhalgarh inscription being carved under royal supervision
panels.action: Artists carve dense lines of Sanskrit praise onto a wall in Kumbhalgarh, while a court poet dictates and a royal official watches, checking each name in the Guhila genealogy.

dialogue.text: By 1460, the Kumbhalgarh Prashasti, composed under Rana Kumbha, gathers scattered memories into one sweeping genealogy. Here, Bappa Rawal stands tall as the fountainhead of Mewar’s line.

i18n.hi: १४६० तक, राणा कुम्भा के दरबार में रची कुम्भलगढ़ प्रशस्ति बिखरी यादों को एक लम्बी वंशावली में पिरो देती है। यहाँ बप्पा रावल मेवाड़ की धारा का पहला बड़ा सिरा बन खड़ा होता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of a scholar comparing Atpur, Ekling, and Kumbhalgarh genealogies laid out side by side
panels.action: A modern historian sits before three large sheets: copies of the Atpur inscription, an Ekling prashasti, and the Kumbhalgarh text, each with certain names underlined and linked by marginal notes.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars like R.V. Somani and Cynthia Talbot lay these records side by side. They trace where names line up and where later poets have filled gaps with honour titles and heroic arcs.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक विद्वान, जैसे आर. वी. सोमानि और सिंथिया टैलबॉट, इन सब अभिलेखों को साथ रखकर पढ़ते हैं। वे देखते हैं कहाँ नाम मिलते हैं, और कहाँ बाद के कवियों ने खाली जगहों को मान-सम्मान और वीर गाथाओं से भरा है।

panels.shot: close-up on Bappa’s face dissolving into multiple possible name-scrolls behind him
panels.action: Bappa’s determined face fills the foreground; behind him, faint overlapping scrolls appear, each bearing a different name—Kalabhoja, Shiladitya, Khumana—none fully solid, all slightly blurred.

dialogue.text: Some identify Bappa with Kalabhoja, some with Shiladitya, others with Khumana. The truth is that the honour-name ‘Bappa Rawal’ floats above at least one real king, but refuses to pin itself down.

i18n.hi: कुछ बप्पा को कलभोज मानते हैं, कुछ शिलादित्य, कुछ खुमाणा। असल में ‘बप्पा रावल’ जैसा मान-नाम कम से कम एक सच्चे राजा पर तैर रहा है, पर खुद को किसी एक पर टिका कर नहीं देता।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bappa seated simply, watching later generations of Guhila rulers in procession
panels.action: Bappa sits cross-legged on stone steps in a dreamlike scene, watching a procession of later Guhila and Mewar rulers ride past him, each more richly adorned than the last.

i18n.hi: नाम धुंधले पड़ जाते हैं। कामों की तरंगें चलती रहती हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of modern Udaipur and the hills of Mewar, with a faint overlay of old inscriptions
panels.action: The cityscape of modern Udaipur and its surrounding hills stretches out under evening light, faint ghostly scripts from the Atpur and Kumbhalgarh inscriptions hovering over the terrain.

dialogue.text: Today, Mewar’s hills hold both stone and song. In its forts and temples, Bappa Rawal lives as symbol, while the early Guhila inscriptions whisper that the dynasty’s rise was slower, more tangled, less certain.

i18n.hi: आज मेवाड़ की पहाड़ियाँ पत्थर भी संभाले हैं और गीत भी। उसकी किलों और देवालयों में बप्पा रावल प्रतीक बनकर जीते हैं, पर पुराने गुहिल शिलालेख फुसफुसाते हैं कि राज की चढ़त धीमी, उलझी और अनिश्चित थी।

panels.shot: final contemplative close-up of Bappa fading into carved stone letters
panels.action: Bappa’s figure stands in three-quarter view, then seems to dissolve into lines of carved Sanskrit letters on a weathered stone slab, as if becoming one with the unnamed founder in the record.

dialogue.text: The legend of Bappa Rawal shows how courts and poets build founders from memory and need; the stone shows that real glory can outlast us even when the name on which it rests is lost.

i18n.hi: बप्पा रावल की कथा दिखाती है कि दरबार और कवि कैसे ज़रूरत और याद से संस्थापक गढ़ते हैं; पत्थर दिखाता है कि सच्‍ची कीर्ति नाम खो जाने पर भी हमारी उम्र से बहुत आगे टिक सकती है।

title_i18n.en: Bappa Rawal and the Founder Nobody Can Name
title_i18n.hi: बप्पा रावल और वो संस्थापक जिसका नाम कोई नहीं जानता

subtitle_i18n.en: In the shadow of Chittor, a nameless founder walks between stone and song
subtitle_i18n.hi: चित्तौड़ की परछाईं में, पत्थर और गीत के बीच एक बेनाम संस्थापक चलता है
